course_description:
Field-based course including pre-excursion lectures, a seven-day field excursion to Heron Island (late September - early October), and laboratory work to illustrate geological processes, morphology & zonation, structure, and sedimentation of coral reefs. Additional fees payable that cover return transport from UQ to Heron Island, accommodation, food, and boating while on Heron Island. There is a quota of 35 students (2026), and students interested in taking this course should complete an Expression of Interest form. For further information, please reach out to the School of the Environment ( environment@enquire.uq.edu.au ).

Modern coral reefs are among the most significant ecosystems on Earth, representing major centres of marine biodiversity, as well as being among the largest geological structures ever made by life on Earth. ERTH3212 is a largely field-based course highlighted by an seven-day field excursion to Heron Island over the in-semester break (26-9-26 to 2-10-26) that aims to illustrate the physical processes, morphology, zonation, structure, & sedimentation on coral reefs within the broader context of modern reef science and environmental protection. The significance of understanding modern reefs for the interpretation of ancient reefs and Earth history also will be emphasized, but the courseﾠprovides fundamental background and practical skills for working on, and the management of, modern reefs. Understanding how reefs form, what critical processes operate and how they have reacted to environmental change in the past is critical for forecasting future reactions to predicted environmental change.

The course also provides an introduction to geological/environmentalﾠresearch procedures and techniques for Earth scientists with interests in modern or ancient reefs and limestone, while providing fundamental context and field experience for biologists and environmental scientists considering careers in coral reef research. Please have a look at our 2012 fieldtrip https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dnLl2r_JeJw .

The field trip will cost approximately $1000 (inclusive of return transport from UQ to Heron Island, accommodation, food, and boating while on Heron Island), in addition to course fees. Eligible students will be informed of payment due dates via email.

A series of lectures and practical contacts will be held in weeks 1 to 9 and then 10 to 12 following the excursion. In some weeks, there may be lectures only, whereas in others weeks there may beﾠlectures and a contact session for more hands-on practical experience. This will be outlined to you before the start of each week. There will also be a swim test conducted in week 2 so we can allocate appropriate resources for everyone in the field and adhere to our risk assessment. The excursion will run during semester break week after week 9.
course_aims: The primary aim of the course is to provide hands-on field experience and an understanding of the main processes involved in modern coral reef development that can assist the interpretation of ancient reefﾠlimestones andﾠprovide a physical process-based contextual background for those continuing in modern or ancient coral reef research, whether geological,ﾠbiological or more environmental.

learning_outcomes.description: Identify the physical and geological processes involved in reef development and geomorphology;
Recognize and understand the causes of the topographic, ecological and sedimentary zonation on modern reef tops;
Carry out independent field work on coral reefs and assess sediment production and dispersal processes on modern reefs;
Propose the morphology, internal structure, and geological evolution of modern reefs in relation to their current morphology;
Describe the formation and evolution of coral cays within the context of global change.
Interpret Earth history and palaeoclimate from fossil reefal limestones by analogy with modern reefs.
Contribute in a professional manner to a team to achieve successful outcomes

assessment_details.title: Project Proposal
assessment_details.task_description: You will be provided with a project scope in Week 3 to be conducted during the Heron Island field trip. During the workshops you can take notes on the methods that can be used in the field and discuss with your teachers what is logistically possible when working on a coral reef. The project proposal is a detailed outline on the planned activities you will conduct with your group in the field. It requires background research, clear methods description, logistical planning, and mapping of the locations of the proposed work. Further details on the structure and requirements for the Project Proposal will be provided in class. While you can discuss and plan with your group this assessment item is submitted individually.
